source.title: Minimum Length of String After Operations

teaching.hint: What can one operation change about the counts of the different letters?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Each operation removes two copies of one letter, preserving its count parity; whenever that letter has at least three copies, another operation is possible.
solution_outline.approach: Count each letter. For every positive count, retain one if it is odd and two if it is even; sum these residual counts.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: Each present letter keeps positive count and its original parity. Counts of all other letters are unchanged by a reduction.
solution_outline.correctness: An operation requires at least three copies and leaves the selected copy, so a present letter cannot disappear. Parity forces at least one odd-count copy or two even-count copies. Whenever three copies remain, a middle occurrence has equal copies on both sides and can remove two. Repeating reaches those bounds independently for every letter, proving the sum attainable and minimal.
solution_outline.complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space for 26 counts.
solution_outline.pitfall: An absent letter contributes zero, and an even positive count cannot be reduced to one or zero.

common_wrong_turns: An absent letter contributes zero, and an even positive count cannot be reduced to one or zero.
source_fidelity_notes: Preserved nonadjacent occurrences, nearest-copy deletions, the surviving selected character, and repeated operations; omitted examples that reveal counts.
